**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. History 2 (0560), Paper 2 - Modern World History Since 1870, ORDINARY LEVEL, JUNE 2020. Duration: Two and a Half Hours.**

Instructions to candidates:

- Answer FOUR Questions.
- TWO questions must be chosen from SECTION A, ONE from SECTION B and ONE other from SECTION C. One of the two questions chosen from SECTION A must be a Starred question.
- Maps should be used to illustrate answers where appropriate. All questions carry equal marks.

SECTION A: in this section, question 1 is compulsory in the sense that the candidate answers either 1A* or 1B* (the two Starred questions) and one other question from the section.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION A: CAMEROON SINCE 1850**

Question one is compulsory. Answer either 1A* or 1B* and one other Question from this section.

**1. Either**

**A\*** Study this text bearing on the scramble, the annexation and German colonial rule in Cameroon (1879 to 1916) and then answer questions a-d which follow. (The maximum mark for each sub-question is indicated in brackets).

> ...The race for the annexation of Cameroon involved Germany and two other world powers....
>
> The signing of the Germano-Duala Treaty of the 1880s put an end to the fierce race for the annexation of Cameroon. Within a couple of days, the German flag was hoisted over Douala, a colonial administrator appointed and Cameroon effectively became a German colony. [line 5] This administrator fell sick and consequently went back to Germany for medical treatment. Thereafter, the necessity for a German colonial government increasingly became apparent and urgent.... In 1885, the first colonial Governor for Cameroon was appointed. He ruled for six years during which German influence and control over the territory was extended from the coast to the interior. This Governor will be remembered for the [line 10] construction of roads, the introduction of plantations along the Cameroon coast etc.
>
> In 1895, a rather brutal and ruthless Administrator was appointed Governor and he ruled the territory for twelve uninterrupted years (1895-1907). Several innovations occurred in Cameroon during this period, some of which include the expansion of plantations, the construction of roads and railways, and the creation of two Concession companies in the [line 15] territory... The very first plantations were established in Victoria.
>
> In 1906 an influential Douala traditional ruler petitioned this Governor to the German government in Berlin. The complaints raised in the petition were investigated and some of them were found to be credible. The reaction of the German Government was swift and uncompromising. The Governor was sacked, prosecuted and severely punished.... [line 20]

*Source: Improvised text by members of the Subject Panel.*

(The "[line n]" marks show the line numbers printed in the margin of the original text, which the questions refer to: line numbers are located by the words quoted in each question.)

Question 1A* b(i)(a) : le « premier administrateur » est donné comme Max Buchner (commissaire impérial par intérim après le départ de Nachtigal, malade et rentré en Allemagne). Certains manuels scolaires avancent un autre nom pour ce premier administrateur ; le nom est à vérifier par un historien avant diffusion. Nachtigal (drapeau hissé le 14 juillet 1884), Julius von Soden (gouverneur 1885-1891), Jesko von Puttkamer (1895-1907) sont ceux de l'historiographie courante.

Question 1A* b(iii) : le sujet ne dit pas quelles réalisations de Soden sont attendues ; le corrigé en propose trois en demandant deux (organisation de l'administration, appui au commerce et aux missions, contrôle de la zone Victoria/Ambas Bay passée à l'Allemagne vers 1887). La date exacte du transfert de la baie d'Ambas est donnée comme « fin des années 1880 ». À accepter : toute réalisation valable hors routes et plantations et hors extension du contrôle vers l'intérieur.

Question 1A* c(ii) : la question dit « the Governor, required in c(ii) above » alors que le gouverneur est demandé en c(i) (coquille du sujet) ; transcrite telle quelle. questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) (i) Apart from the European power mentioned in the extract, name one other power that was involved in the race for the control of Cameroon in the 1870s and 1880s (Line 1).

(ii) In which year was the Germano-Duala Treaty (line 2) signed?

(iii) Name two Cameroonians who signed the treaty mentioned in a(ii) above.

[1+1+2 marks]
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Another power in the race.** Britain (Great Britain). The extract says that the race involved Germany "and two other world powers": these were Britain and France, so either one is correct. Britain was the strongest rival because her traders, her Baptist missionaries and her consuls had been on the Cameroon coast for decades, and the Duala chiefs had asked her for protection.

**(ii) Year of the treaty.** 1884. The Germano-Duala Treaty was signed at Douala on 12 July 1884 (the German flag was hoisted on 14 July 1884).

**(iii) Two Cameroonians who signed.** King Bell (Ndumbe Lobe Bell) and King Akwa (Dika Mpondo Akwa), the two leading Duala rulers. (The German side was represented by the agents of the Hamburg trading firms Woermann and Jantzen and Thormählen, Eduard Schmidt and Johannes Voss; Gustav Nachtigal, the Imperial Commissioner, arrived at the same time and confirmed the arrangement.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) (i) Identify the German official who (a) was appointed first Administrator for Cameroon (line 5) and (b) hoisted the German flag over Douala (line 3).

(ii) Give the name of the German official who was appointed first Colonial Governor (line 8).

(iii) State two major achievements of the Governor mentioned in b(ii) above excluding achievements highlighted in the text.

[2+1+2 marks]
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)(a) First Administrator.** Dr Max Buchner. After the treaty, Nachtigal left the coast and Buchner, an explorer and doctor, was left in charge as acting Imperial Commissioner (administrator); he fell ill and returned to Germany, as the extract says. (Some school texts give another name for this first administrator: see the note on uncertainties.)

**(i)(b) The official who hoisted the flag.** Gustav Nachtigal, the German Imperial Commissioner for West Africa. He arrived at Douala on 11 July 1884 on the gunboat *Möwe*, the treaty was signed on 12 July and he hoisted the German flag on 14 July 1884.

**(ii) First Colonial Governor.** Julius von Soden (Baron von Soden), Governor from 1885 to 1891 (the "six years" of the text).

**(iii) Two achievements other than roads, plantations and the extension of control inland.** Any two of:
1. He set up the first organised German colonial government: government offices, a small civil service, courts and a police force, and he began to collect customs duties to finance the colony.
2. He encouraged German trading companies and missionary work (the Basel Mission took over from the Baptist Mission in 1886), so that trade and education spread.
3. He made German control stronger on the coast, including the Victoria and Ambas Bay area, which passed from British to German hands in the late 1880s.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) (i) Name the German Governor (line 12) famous for acts of brutality and ruthlessness.

(ii) Write down two acts of brutality that were associated with this colonial Governor who took up office in 1895.

(iii) Name the two Concession companies (line 15) that the Governor, required in c(ii) above, created.

[1+2+2 marks]
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) The brutal Governor.** Jesko von Puttkamer, Governor of Kamerun from 1895 to 1907 (in the text, "twelve uninterrupted years").

**(ii) Two acts of brutality.** Any two of:
1. Flogging of Africans (men and women) with the hippopotamus-hide whip as a normal punishment, which was one of the charges made against him.
2. Forced labour and forced recruitment of porters and plantation workers, who were badly treated and badly fed.
3. Punitive military expeditions against villages that resisted German rule or refused to supply labour, in which villages were burnt and people killed.
4. Seizing land and cattle from the people for the plantations and the concession companies.

**(iii) The two Concession companies.** The Gesellschaft Süd-Kamerun (South Cameroon Company) and the Gesellschaft Nordwest-Kamerun (North-West Cameroon Company), created in 1898-1899. They received huge areas of land and the right to trade in rubber and ivory in exchange for a share of their profits.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(d) (i) Apart from Victoria (line 16), suggest one other coastal settlement where plantations were established.

(ii) Name two cash crops that were grown in the plantations.

(iii) Why do you think that the very first plantations were established in Victoria (line 16)?

[1+2+3 marks]
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Another coastal settlement.** Any one of Bota, Bibundi, Idenau, Tiko or Mukonje, all on the slopes of Mount Cameroon near the coast.

**(ii) Two cash crops.** Any two of cocoa, bananas, rubber, oil palm and coffee. (Cocoa, bananas and rubber were the best known on the German plantations.)

**(iii) Why Victoria came first.** Three reasons:
1. The volcanic soils of the slopes of Mount Cameroon are very fertile and the rainfall is heavy, which suits tropical cash crops.
2. Victoria was a port on the coast, so the produce could be exported to Europe easily and machines and supplies could be landed cheaply.
3. Victoria had been founded in 1858 by the Baptist missionary Alfred Saker and was already a settled community with some roads, workers and know-how, and the nearby Bakweri villages could provide land and, under pressure, labour.
